title: Príncipe v1.0.1 — security patch + calibration refresh
summary: Patch release closes two Medium security findings and refreshes the Leg-2 calibration baseline.
body: v1.0.1 is a recommended update for all self-hosters. It closes two Medium findings from the security audit: news-body content is now sanitised against XSS, and the fetch layer's SSRF guard is hardened against DNS-rebinding by pinning TCP connections to the pre-resolved IP. The Leg-2 calibration baseline has also been recomputed (12 responses). Run `bin/stop.sh` before pulling the update for a clean shutdown.
why: Drafted from a recent product change.

title: PDF exports now match the full decision card
summary: Exported reports now include ranked top-3 objections, the 'what the panel almost missed' blind spot, and the Contested flag.
body: The PDF export previously lagged the in-app view, showing only a single legacy objection. It now renders the ranked top-3 objections, the adversarial review's blind-spot finding, and the Contested minority-stronger flag — identical to what you see on screen. Single-asterisk emphasis (`*like this*`) also renders correctly in exports after a formatting fix.
why: Drafted from a recent product change.

title: Panel gains a mandate (organisational authority) axis
summary: A fourth persona dimension — reactive bolt-on → embedded → strategic CEO-of-security — now shapes every panel run.
body: The synthetic panel previously varied CISOs across three disposition axes. A fourth axis has been added covering organisational authority and program maturity, distributed roughly 40% reactive / 38% embedded / 22% strategic, independent of the existing axes. Calibration-neutral on the global-survey benchmark set (MAE holds at ~17.8 pp). The adversarial peer-review pass (three reviewers from distinct lenses, challenging the ranked objections before the final decision) also shipped in this cycle.
why: Drafted from a recent product change.

title: Version number now visible in-app, plus a 'Stay in touch' card
summary: The app now shows its version on the launch splash and in About, and a new card links out to community channels without phoning home.
body: You can now confirm exactly which build you're running from the launch splash or the About footer — both pull from the same source as the git tag. A zero-call-home 'Stay in touch' card has been added for community links. The Príncipe logo in exported PDF reports is now also a clickable link.
